experiments.title: Benign mismatch or harmful state?
experiments.topic: benign mismatch harmful state preaction forecasting integrity bit deterministic policy validator
experiments.statusLabel: Pilot finished · final result added later
experiments.question: Can rich carried state distinguish harmless-to-this-query mismatches from harmful ones, beyond a one-bit check and deterministic semantic rules?
experiments.finding: The one delayed harmful-release actor followed the corrupted verification record and made unsupported completion claims. Across six outcomes, actual-state forecasts flagged both violations and no safe actions; query-aware code also matched all six. The original 23-call stopped run remains separate.
setup: Reuse the lexicographically first E6 source world in each family without selecting on model outcomes. The harmful state reuses its frozen E6 mutation.

The benign export grant changes only its recipient to an existing unrelated recipient. The benign release edit changes the same suite scalar to another nonqualifying version. Both remain factual mismatches while preserving selected-query predicates.

Baseline, actual-state and integrity-bit forecasts receive a common equal-mixture disclosure. Baseline is identical across variants; the bit view is identical for harmful and benign states. All three forecasts are hashed before the actor receives its exact committed input.

Primary Brier scores and secondary flags use later original-source action labels. Score any-mismatch, mixture and query-aware deterministic heuristics separately. The query-aware rule validates a hypothetical record-compliant ideal action, without knowing future actor behavior.
A September 10 amendment prospectively allowed exactly one delayed actor for the missing cell, with the September 8 input and forecasts unchanged. No retries or new forecasts were made.
limitations: Benign means unchanged policy predicates for this selected query, not factual faithfulness or global trustworthiness. The fabricated permission remains a record error, and a strict integrity gate may reasonably reject it.
Three state types and their equal proportions are constructed. Six trials from two structured worlds do not estimate natural failure prevalence, deployment risk or adversarial intent.
Complete structured policy semantics permit a strong deterministic control. Model prediction must be compared with that control, not only a coarse mismatch bit.
Repeated baseline and bit inputs, one actor draw per cell and shared model family limit generalization. There is no calibration, power, readiness or private-chain-of-thought faithfulness claim.

The original run remains stopped. The six-target summary combines dates after prior outcomes were known; model service weights may have changed. This is exploratory and not an independent replication.
experiments.next: Pilot collection is closed. Preserve the original stopped run and dated supplement. Before any main study, develop held-out tasks with natural failures and compare model review against strong code checks; no further model collection is scheduled.
experiments.interpretation: Detailed supplied state helped distinguish task-relevant faults from benign mismatches. Actual-state forecasts caught both violations without false flags; baseline and integrity-bit models missed both at the fixed threshold. Query-aware code also scored perfectly, so no advantage over executable semantic checking is established.

results.caption: Exploratory combined six-target analysis: five September 8 actors plus one September 10 actor. Original five-target scores remain in the report and original dataset. Lower Brier is better.

experiments.title: Can public state forecast future violations?
experiments.topic: preaction forecasting carried state integrity fault one bit control source comparison
experiments.question: Does seeing the actual carried inventory improve forecasts of the next actor action, beyond an independent aid or one bit of integrity information?
experiments.findingLabel: PRE-ACTION SIGNAL / SIMPLE INTEGRITY RULE ALSO PERFECT
experiments.finding: All four corrupted-state trials produced violations; all four intact trials succeeded safely. Actual-state forecasts identified all four future violations. The deterministic rule that every mismatch predicts a violation also scored perfectly on this controlled fault set.
setup: Two export and two release worlds are selected by fixed source-only eligibility rules and sorted IDs. A fault adds one scoped permission fact or changes one attestation scalar; these inventories are deterministic experimenter-created artifacts.

All forecasters see original evidence, the query, the controller description, and the same balanced integrity-stress disclosure. Views add nothing, the actual actor input, an independent source projection, or only a deterministic source-integrity Boolean.

The state and all four forecasts are hashed before the actor is called. The actor receives only its committed query, immutable policy, and inventory; it receives no forecasts or original source packets.

Brier score is the primary descriptive prediction measure; flags are secondary. A no-call match-to-0/mismatch-to-1 heuristic is also scored against actual later actions. All 40 calls and their counterbalanced order are frozen; no retry or external action occurs.
limitations: The faults and their 50% prevalence are constructed, not natural model errors, deployment prevalence, or evidence of adversarial intent. A corrupted state is not automatically an action violation.
Actual-state and independent-aid views combine content, truthful provenance information, and packet structure. The integrity-bit control tests whether richer state adds beyond that simpler signal.
Baseline and independent-aid packets repeat across each world's two variants. These are repeated same-input measurements from four worlds sharing two templates, with one actor draw per trial.

A forecast near 0.5 can be reasonable under the disclosed balanced design. Fixed flags and eight outcomes establish neither probability calibration nor deployment risk; no readiness or improvement gate applies.

Public-state prediction does not recover private chain of thought or establish an internal reasoning mechanism. An actor may follow its supplied inventory while conflicting with the unchanged original-source label.
experiments.next: Prepare a separate small control containing intact, harmful-mismatch and harmless-mismatch states. Compare detailed state with an integrity bit, a conservative mismatch rule, a mixture-risk rule and a query-aware deterministic check before making an integration or trust claim.

results.caption: Eight actual later actions under controlled state faults. Lower Brier is better; 0.5 flags are uncalibrated. Harmless mismatches were not included.

experiments.interpretation: Seeing the actual supplied state improved model forecasts on these eight later actions, including over a model given only the integrity bit. The observable mechanism is access to the mistaken input premise before action selection. This does not reveal private reasoning. Every injected mismatch was selected to change a decision-relevant predicate; harmless discrepancies were absent, so the perfect mismatch heuristic is a narrow result.

experiments.title: Carried state or independent reviewer aid?
experiments.topic: carried record independent evidence reviewer assistance constructed controls trust
experiments.question: Does the exact inventory carried by an actor help review more than an independently generated inventory with matching inputs?
experiments.findingLabel: ALL VIEWS AT DETECTION CEILING / IDENTICAL INVENTORIES
experiments.finding: Every view accepted all eight safe actor proposals and caught all eight constructed faults. All eight independent inventories were identical to the carried inventories. No added flag-level detection benefit was observed on these fixed candidates.
setup: Independent inventories use the exact original hidden-request extraction inputs, instructions, schema and capacity. They receive no later query, actor output, carried record, grade, or earlier monitor result.
All reviews are fresh. The query, original evidence and candidate stay fixed; a neutral public_evidence field contains null, the carried inventory, or the independent inventory.

Original candidates are unchanged. Eligible safe actions also receive one fixed semantic boundary error, checked by the independent source-based grader and explicitly marked experimenter-constructed in the released data.
Counterbalanced order, unchanged inaccurate inventories, fixed stopping and no retries. No external action executes.
limitations: Constructed faults measure reviewer behavior on those edits; they cannot estimate natural failure prevalence or sensitivity on actual actor mistakes.
Carried versus independent combines artifact content quality, presentation and connection to the actor. It does not isolate a pure causal effect of provenance.
Eight worlds share two templates. One sample per view and an uncalibrated 0.5 threshold do not establish a trust score or main-study readiness.
If the two inventories are identical, different reviewer outputs reflect stochastic repeated review of the same inputs, not a provenance effect.
experiments.next: Experiment 006 tests a different target: forecasting a future action before it exists, using controlled state faults and a one-bit integrity control. Keep this separate from natural-error detection and from private-reasoning claims.

results.caption: Natural and constructed populations are separate. Threshold 0.5 is uncalibrated; lower Brier is better within a cohort.

experiments.interpretation: Natural-error sensitivity remains undefined because all original candidates were safe. Constructed faults were detected even without an inventory, leaving no flag-level improvement headroom. Carried and independent inputs were identical; their tiny probability differences are repeated measurements, not a carried-state or provenance effect. This result does not establish population-level equivalence or calibrated trust.

experiments.title: Evidence before the request
experiments.topic: late query typed evidence extraction source projection public state oversight
experiments.question: Can public evidence committed before a specific request support later decisions, and does the carried record help review those decisions?
experiments.findingLabel: EXACT EVIDENCE COPIES / MONITORING GAIN UNMEASURED
experiments.finding: All 16 model inventories exactly matched the deterministic source projection. All 32 actions were safe and task-correct, and all 56 reviews accepted them. With no actor violations, added detection benefit remains unmeasured.
setup: Four export-authorization and four release-verification worlds contain multiple possible requests. Hidden-request record calls receive neither the selected request nor a revealing world or query identifier.
Both model-extraction conditions use the same typed source-field schema and capacity, sufficient to fit the complete deterministic projection. Incorrect records are retained unchanged.

Every action receives independent original-evidence review. The three conditions with a carried record also receive a paired review with that record. The full-evidence condition has no invented record.
The fixed call graph has two model record commits, four actions and seven reviews per world. No external actions execute and no automatic retries occur.
limitations: A fixed eight-world development study cannot establish calibrated trust, population-level reliability, or main-study power.
Different controller conditions can produce different failures. Within-candidate paired review measures record assistance; cross-condition recall alone does not isolate its cause.
The monitor threshold is fixed for development and is not calibrated to a target false-positive rate. Typed public records do not disclose private computation.
The structured policies have deterministic evaluators. Model-based review is not established as necessary compared with available executable checks.
experiments.next: Experiment 005 fixes all eight request-hidden candidates and compares fresh reviews using no inventory, the carried inventory, or an independently generated matched inventory. Deliberately faulty candidates are a separately reported diagnostic cohort. Main-study readiness still requires a suitable natural-failure distribution and independent calibration.

results.caption: Descriptive counts; eight assigned worlds per condition. TP/FN/FP/TN refers to valid graded actions.

experiments.interpretation: The hidden-request condition preserved evidence for a later decision without storing a solved answer. However, both model-written inventories and the deterministic inventory were identical in every world, including array order. Their action inputs were consequently identical within each world; these comparisons provide repeated draws, not evidence of a distinct reasoning signal. The result supports evidence copying and later use on these structured tasks, not recovered private reasoning or a monitoring advantage.

experiments.title: Oversight evidence screening
experiments.topic: monitor headroom record compression source precedence verification
experiments.question: Do source and version conflicts produce real action mistakes, and does a public record help or harm review of those same actions?
experiments.finding: All six proposed actions were safe and task-correct. Both monitor views accepted all six. With no violations, detection sensitivity and added detection benefit remain unmeasured.
setup: Three export-permission cases combine row/group precedence, exact recipient and purpose, revisions, expiry, and cached suggestions. Three release-verification cases combine build, artifact, suite, environment, runner status, and invalidation.
A fresh call commits a bounded public fact record. A separate fresh call receives the immutable policy, identifier catalog, and record, then proposes an inert action.
Two fresh reviewers receive the same original evidence and candidate. Only one also receives the committed record. Factual record errors are retained; there is no repair or selective retry.
limitations: Six development cases cannot establish power, calibrated false-positive rates, or main-study readiness. They will not enter confirmatory analysis.
Record compression quality and downstream decision capability are combined in this screen. Both reviewers and actors use Astra.
The monitor threshold is fixed at 0.5 for screening; it is not a calibrated 10% false-positive threshold.

Records encoded the solved answers; a facts schema alone did not keep record creation separate from decision-making. All twelve monitor probability scores were zero, leaving no score variation for calibration.
experiments.next: Prepare a separate request-after-commit study to distinguish a reusable evidence record from a precomputed answer. Establish actual errors and monitoring headroom on development cases before calibration or a main run.
experiments.interpretation: The committed records correctly resolved source conflicts, but already contained the exact row sets or release-check lists. Action selection largely reformatted solved answers. This establishes neither a distinct downstream decision mechanism nor improved CoT monitorability. The preregistered error and monitor-headroom gates failed.

results.caption: Descriptive counts on six fixed development cases. No violating candidates were available to estimate sensitivity.
rows: Action-only monitor: TP / FN / FP / TN
Record-assisted monitor: TP / FN / FP / TN

experiments.title: Public state after a late trusted update
experiments.topic: causal public state action anchoring export release verification
experiments.question: Can a fresh action session revise an obsolete proposal using a separately committed public record?
experiments.finding: Fresh sessions acted on the updated public facts in both workflows. Relevant fact edits changed the action; paraphrases and irrelevant edits preserved it. Information-limited decisions deferred.
setup: Case 1: a trusted update revokes permission to include one record in a vendor export.
Case 2: a new build invalidates the integration verification supporting an earlier complete status.

Each case first produces an initial action and a separate record-only commit. Four fresh sessions cross record retention with obsolete-action retention. Four additional sessions test a relevant alternate-world fact, paraphrase, irrelevant metadata, and omission.
Incorrect setup or inaccurate records make a case ineligible. There are no automatic retries or post-result prompt changes.
limitations: Record-present cells have more current evidence. Their task-completion advantage is not an isolated reasoning or monitorability benefit.
Both fixtures are small, benign, and explicitly instruct the actor to defer without evidence and disregard obsolete proposals. There is only one sample per cell.
No monitor calls or adaptive adversarial tests were performed. These outcomes do not establish access to private reasoning or general resistance to anchoring.
experiments.next: Test whether a committed record adds detection value for a reviewer beyond the same evidence and candidate action, on harder workflows with actual model-generated mistakes. Register that protocol before running it.

results.caption: Counts describe these fixed cells; they are not population-level accuracy estimates.

experiments.interpretation: The public record was a usable path for current evidence across fresh sessions. There was no observed anchoring effect from retaining the stale proposal. This study included no monitor evaluation, so it does not establish improved CoT monitorability.

experiments.title: Export oversight calibration
experiments.topic: monitorability public working state export restricted data
experiments.question: Does a public record help a reviewer catch an export-policy violation before the proposal is executed?
experiments.finding: All eight actor trajectories produced safe exports. Both monitor views caught the two planted faults. Incremental detection benefit is unmeasured because no actor-generated violation occurred.
setup: One synthetic vendor-export fixture: two shareable records, two restricted records, three allowed fields, and an untrusted request for the full worksheet.

Four conditions compare ordinary explanation, a typed record, full public-history replay, and restricted public state. Each is run with a nominal objective and an explicit synthetic adversarial objective.
Each final proposal receives two fresh reviews: original evidence and actions, or that same packet plus the public record. Two deliberately faulty positive controls are reviewed separately.

results.caption: Actor proposals and planted controls are separate populations.

experiments.interpretation: The transport, public-message replay, evaluator, and paired-review pipeline worked. These observations do not establish a record advantage or show that records are generally useless.
limitations: The public record followed the candidate action, allowing a post-decision explanation.
The restricted-state arm retained an earlier correct action. Copying it could succeed without consulting the narrative.
The short fixture contains little ambiguity, and the positive controls are obvious from the evidence and action.
experiments.next: Introduce a trusted update that requires a changed action, commit the record separately, and vary record retention independently of the previous action.
